title: The robed monster and its hands
summary: The robed monster in R.E.P.O. attacks with hands that are audible on their own: the game gives it an idle hand sound, an aggressive one, and a separate attack from underneath.
body: The robed monster does not have a head like the others. Its eye has a location of its own, and the thing you see is a robe with an end piece that trails behind on a spring with a source and a target.
It waits and then moves. Its idle time has a shortest and a longest value, so it does not act on the same rhythm twice, and it turns on a rotation spring rather than snapping to face you.
It follows one player in particular. There is a loop sound for that, with a flag for whether the loop is playing, which is how the game can tell you that you are the one being followed.

Its hands are audible by themselves. There is an idle hand sound and an aggressive one, each with a flag recording whether it is playing, so the game knows when a hand is resting and when it is about to close.
It attacks twice over. There is an attack, and there is a separate attack from underneath, and each of those has a sound for the player and a sound for the rest of the crew.
Everything else about it is the standard monster set: idle breaks, being hurt, dying and being stunned with a start and a loop, along with a vision point of its own.
It arrives and leaves with effects. There are teleport particles, spawn particles and death particles, so its appearance and its end are both visible rather than instantaneous.

There is also a version that does not go away. A persistent robe exists with a constant particle of its own, which is how the game can keep one of them present without it being the same object as the one hunting you.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the face-and-hands sheet the robed monster is drawn from.
What this entry does not tell you: how much damage a hand does, how long it waits between attacks, or how far it can reach. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Its eye has a location of its own rather than being part of a head.
Its idle time has a shortest and a longest value.
It turns on a rotation spring and its end piece trails on a spring with a source and a target.
It follows a player with a loop sound and a flag for whether that loop is playing.
Its hands have an idle sound and an aggressive one, each with a flag for whether it is playing.
It has an ordinary attack and an attack from underneath, each with a player and a level version.
Idle breaks, being hurt, dying and being stunned each have sounds, with a start and a loop for the stun.
facts.evidence: identifiers: sfxIdleBreak, sfxHurt, sfxDeath, sfxStunStart, sfxStunLoop

facts.claim: It has a vision point and teleport, spawn and death particles.
facts.evidence: identifiers: EnemyRobeAnim, visionTransform, teleportParticles, spawnParticles, deathParticles

facts.claim: A persistent version of the robe exists with a constant particle.
